arxiv-2106-14221.title: Can a liquid drop on a substrate be in equilibrium with saturated vapor?
arxiv-2106-14221.creator: E. S. Benilov
arxiv-2106-14221.description: Abstract It is well-known that liquid and saturated vapor, separated by a flat interface in an unbounded space, are in equilibrium. One would similarly expect a liquid drop, sitting on a flat substrate, to be in equilibrium with the vapor surrounding it. Yet, it is not: as shown in this work, the drop evaporates.

arxiv-2212-05212.creator: Nguyen Anh Dao
arxiv-2212-05212.description: Abstract . Our main purpose is to establish Gagliardo–Nirenberg type inequalities using fractional homogeneous Sobolev spaces, and homogeneous Besov spaces. In particular, we extend some of the results obtained by the authors in [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 7 , 16 , 21 ] . 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 46E35; Secondary 46B70. 1.

arxiv-2305-04423.title: Robust Power Allocation for UAV-aided ISAC Systems with Uncertain Location Sensing Errors
arxiv-2305-04423.creator: Junchang Sun, Shuai Ma, Ruixin Yang, Tingting Yang, Shiyin Li
arxiv-2305-04423.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Junchang Sun, Shuai Ma, Ruixin Yang, Tingting Yang, Shiyin Li. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) holds immense potential in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems for the Internet of Things (IoT). In this paper, we propose a UAV-aided ISAC framework and investigate three robust power allocation schemes. First, we derive an explicit expression of the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) based on time-of-arrival (ToA) estimation, which serves as the performance metric for location sensing.

arxiv-2501-01088.title: Detecting high-dimensional entanglement by randomized product projections
arxiv-2501-01088.creator: Jin-Min Liang, Shuheng Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Qiongyi He
arxiv-2501-01088.description: Abstract The characterization of high-dimensional entanglement plays a crucial role in the field of quantum information science. Conventional entanglement criteria measuring coherent superpositions of multiple basis states face experimental bottlenecks on most physical platforms due to limited multi-channel control. Here, we introduce a practically efficient detection strategy based on randomized product projections.

pmc-10541502.title: Gut-targeted nanoparticles deliver specifically targeted antimicrobial peptides against Clostridium perfringens infections
pmc-10541502.creator: Bocheng Xu, Weike Shaoyong, Lin Wang, Chen Yang, Tingjun Chen, Xiao Jiang, Rong Yan, Zipeng Jiang, Pan Zhang, Mingliang Jin, Yizhen Wang
pmc-10541502.description: Specifically targeted antimicrobial peptides (STAMPs) are novel alternatives to antibiotics, whereas the development of STAMPs for colonic infections is hindered by limited de novo design efficiency and colonic bioavailability. In this study, we report an efficient de novo STAMP design strategy that combines a traversal design, machine learning model, and phage display technology to identify STAMPs against Clostridium perfringens.

pmc-11600916.title: Out of Hospital Bystander CPR Rates in Baltimore City, Maryland, 2020-2022, Compared to State and National Rates: A Preliminary Report
pmc-11600916.creator: Christian Angelo I Ventura, Benjamin J Lawner, Jennifer E Guyther, Jason Gullion
pmc-11600916.description: This preliminary study was a rapid retrospective analysis of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) cases from Baltimore City between January 2020 and December 2022, using data from the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival. Of the 1,282 cases in 2022, 27.4% received bystander CPR compared to 40.7% in Maryland and 40.8% nationwide.

pmc-11608310.title: Black Tea drinks with inulin and dextrin reduced postprandial plasma glucose fluctuations in patients with type 2 diabetes: an acute, randomized, placebo-controlled, single-blind crossover study
pmc-11608310.creator: Si Chen, Danfeng Peng, Yingyi Shan, Fengjing Liu, Ronghui Du, Yuqian Bao, Haoyong Yu, Yinfang Tu
pmc-11608310.description: BackgroundThis study evaluated the effects of black tea drinks with inulin and dextrin (BTID) on postprandial plasma glucose (PG) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).MethodsAn acute, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover clinical trial was carried out on T2DM patients.

pmc-11656007.title: Realization of high-end PET devices that assist conventional PET devices in improving image quality via diffusion modeling
pmc-11656007.creator: Qiyang Zhang, Chao Zhou, Xu Zhang, Wei Fan, Hairong Zheng, Dong Liang, Zhanli Hu
pmc-11656007.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeThis study aimed to implement high-end positron emission tomography (PET) equipment to assist conventional PET equipment in improving image quality via a distribution learning-based diffusion model.MethodsA diffusion model was first trained on a dataset of high-quality (HQ) images acquired by a high-end PET device (uEXPLORER scanner), and the quality of the conventional PET images was later improved on the basis of this trained model built on null-space constraints. Data from 180 patients were used in this study.

pmc-11712066.title: A Neuroimaging Perspective on Familial Alzheimer’s Functional Data through Bayesian Eyes
pmc-11712066.creator: Alice Grazia, Martin Dyrba, Pomara Nunzio, Anna GM Temp, Michel J Grothe, Stefan Teipel
pmc-11712066.description: BackgroundFamilial Alzheimer’s disease research necessitates innovative methodologies to disentangle the intricate relationships between genetic factors and neuroimaging measures. Traditional frequentist approaches, often hampered by small sample sizes in this population and challenges in incorporating prior knowledge transparently, may limit the robustness of findings.

pmc-12859898.title: The mediating role of thriving at work between emotional labor and presenteeism: a comparison between psychiatric nurses with and without sleep disturbances
pmc-12859898.creator: Jianing Li, Xiaolian Li, Yaoying Chen, Mei Chen, Wen Shi, Huijun Huang
pmc-12859898.description: BackgroundEmotional labor is a significant component of healthcare work, yet the mechanisms linking it to presenteeism are not fully understood. Existing research has centered on negative mediating pathways, leaving the potential role of the positive psychological state of thriving at work underexplored.

pmc-13049788.title: A rare coexistence of hypoplasia of the middle cerebral artery with aortic arch origin of the vertebral artery: a case report and analysis of hemodynamic vulnerability
pmc-13049788.creator: Jiazhen Li, Yinbao Hu
pmc-13049788.description: BackgroundCongenital cerebrovascular anomalies, such as middle cerebral artery hypoplasia and vertebral artery with an aortic arch origin, are well-documented in isolation but exceedingly rare in combination. Their coexistence may critically disrupt cerebral hemodynamics, yet clinical implications remain poorly characterized, highlighting the novelty of this case.

pmc-13145435.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A647 FROM TOKENISM TO PARTNERSHIP: OVERCOMING RECRUITMENT AND GOVERNANCE BARRIERS TO INVOLVING PEOPLE WITH STROKE AS RESEARCH PARTNERS
pmc-13145435.creator: Marina Charalambous
pmc-13145435.description: Background and aimsDespite increasing endorsement of patient and public involvement (PPI) in stroke research, people with stroke are frequently involved in limited or consultative roles. Recruitment challenges, communication barriers, and restrictive research governance processes often result in tokenistic involvement rather than meaningful partnership.

pmc-13299361.title: Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cells in Inflammatory Arthritis
pmc-13299361.creator: Daniel R. McDougle, James J. Moon, David A. Fox
pmc-13299361.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are a heterogeneous group of immature myeloid cell populations with potent immunosuppressive activity. MDSCs accumulate during states of chronic inflammation in response to inflammatory cytokine signaling that triggers emergency myelopoiesis in the bone marrow. In rheumatoid arthritis and experimental models of inflammatory arthritis, MDSCs were initially thought to serve as a regulatory checkpoint that limits excessive inflammation.

pmc-13323437.title: Cabozantinib and atezolizumab for recurrent or metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after platinum-based chemotherapy failure: a single-arm phase II study and biomarker analysis
pmc-13323437.creator: Hung-Yang Kuo, Ta-Chen Huang, Chien-Huai Chuang, Tsung-Che Wu, Yen-Lin Huang, Chia-Chi Lin, Jang-Ming Lee, Jhe-Cyuan Guo, Chih-Hung Hsu
pmc-13323437.description: PurposeAnti-PD-1 immune-checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are approved for treating patients with recurrent or metastatic (R/M) esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) who have failed platinum-based chemotherapy. However, their efficacy as monotherapy remains limited. We hypothesized that adding cabozantinib, a multikinase inhibitor with antiangiogenic and immunomodulatory properties, could enhance the therapeutic efficacy of atezolizumab, an anti-PD-L1 ICI, in patients with R/M ESCC.

pmc-13352279.title: Heterogeneous Composite Design and 3D Printing Parameter Optimization of Al2O3 Ceramic Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Structures
pmc-13352279.creator: Wei Liu, Kai Ren, Jinglei Zhou, Jinchao Zhao, Qi Liu, Liang Chen, Shanchen Zhou, Zongbo Zheng, Lei Tu, Yanlong Cao
pmc-13352279.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) Al2O3 ceramic structures hold significant potential for applications in biomedical engineering, catalytic systems, and thermal management technologies, which can be fabricated with high precision using vat photopolymerization-based digital light processing (DLP). However, conventional homogeneous designs for TPMS often do not fully meet advanced performance requirements, while the curing depth, a key parameter governing the dimensional accuracy and mechanical performance, has not been thoroughly investigated.

pmc-13378550.title: Ridge-assisted micro positioning of cells in a channel
pmc-13378550.creator: Adriana Payan-Medina, Victor R. Putaturo, Sajad R. Bazaz, Quinn E. Cunneely, Varun Kulkarni, Mehmet Toner, Avanish Mishra
pmc-13378550.description: The ability to deterministically and precisely control the lateral position of focused cell streams within a microchannel enables a wide range of biomedical applications, including cell concentration, sorting, and sensing. By leveraging engineered microvortices generated by channel ridges and fluidic lift forces, we present a microfluidic method for deterministically positioning focused cell streams to desired streamlines.
